title: Toxicity study of UV/ZnO treated solution containing Reactive blue 29 using Daphnia magna as a biological indicator
author: Dehghani, Mahmoodi, et al.

steps.title: Prepare synthetic freshwater medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve MgSO4 (246 mg/L), NaHCO3 (192 mg/L), CaSO4 (120 mg/L) and KCl (8 mg/L) in deionized water to obtain hard water (hardness 168 mg CaCO3/L, alkalinity 115 mg CaCO3/L) with pH 7.5; let the solution stand for at least two weeks before use.

steps.title: Acclimate Daphnia magna culture
steps.instruction: Transfer the laboratory D. magna culture to the synthetic freshwater, feed algae, replace the medium weekly, aerate gently with an aquarium air pump, and continuously monitor dissolved oxygen (>5 mg/L, ~90 % saturation), pH (≈7.5) and temperature (~25 °C) throughout the acclimation period.

steps.title: Collect and wash neonates
steps.instruction: Using a plastic pipette, collect neonates younger than 24 h; wash them in diluted synthetic water for 5 min, repeat the wash three times; then feed them with phytoplankton and a slurry of yeast, Cerophyll and trout chow at 18.5 mg dry weight per litre.

substeps.instruction: Collect neonates (<24 h) with plastic pipette
Wash three times, 5 min each, in diluted water
Feed with phytoplankton and yeast‑Cerophyll‑trout chow slurry (18.5 mg DW/L)

steps.title: Prepare ZnO adsorbent dosages
steps.instruction: Make ZnO nanoparticle solutions at 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 mg L⁻¹; add each to Reactive Blue 29 stock solution (initial concentration 100 mg L⁻¹); stir the mixtures on a magnetic stirrer for 20 min in a dark place.

steps.title: UV‑treat dye‑adsorbent mixture
steps.instruction: Transfer each stirred mixture to an ultraviolet reactor, cover the reactor with aluminum foil, and expose it to a Phillips HPLN 125 W lamp (λ ≥ 254 nm) with constant mixing to prevent nanoparticle sedimentation; keep the exposure for the predetermined duration.

steps.title: Prepare exposure beakers
steps.instruction: Soak new beakers in 1 % nitric acid, rinse them thoroughly with synthetic water, label one beaker as control (0 mg L⁻¹) and the others for test concentrations of 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 75 and 100 mg L⁻¹, then add the appropriate volume of the UV‑treated solution to each beaker.

substeps.instruction: Add UV‑treated solution to each beaker

steps.title: Add neonates to beakers
steps.instruction: Introduce ten D. magna neonates into each exposure beaker.

steps.title: Incubate and monitor exposures
steps.instruction: Incubate the beakers at ~25 °C, continuously monitor pH (≈7.5) and dissolved oxygen (>5 mg L⁻¹, ~90 % saturation), and make observations at 24, 48, 72 and 96 h.

steps.title: Assess mortality and record data
steps.instruction: At 24 and 48 h (and later time points), gently shake each beaker and count individuals that do not swim within 15 s as dead; perform each concentration in duplicate, ensure control mortality ≤10 %, and calculate LC₅₀ from the mortality data.

substeps.instruction: Count immobile individuals (no swimming within 15 s) as dead
